items.title: How to Get a Salon Worthy Blowout at Home
items.summary: A great blowout isn't just about technique. It's about working with your hair type, protecting your hair from heat, and creating a routine that builds smoothness, volume, and shine from the start. Whether your hair is straight, wavy, curly, or coily, understanding how heat changes your hair's structure can help you achieve longer-lasting results with less damage. Key Takeaways The best blowouts start with clean, conditioned hair that's matched to your hair type. Heat protection is essential for helping reduce moisture loss and protecting the hair cuticle. Drying your hair in sections creates smoother, longer-lasting results. Allowing each section to cool helps lock in shape and volume. Lightweight styling products help support movement, reduce frizz, and improve longevity without weighing hair down. Why Hair Prep Matters Your blowout starts long before you pick up a blow dryer. Healthy-looking blowouts begin with hair that's clean, hydrated, and conditioned for your hair type. Product buildup, excess oil, or dehydrated hair can all affect how your style looks and how long it lasts. Wash your hair with your Function of Beauty Custom Shampoo and Conditioner, personalized for your hair type and goals. If your goal is hydration, frizz control, or strengthening, your formula is designed to support those needs before styling even begins. After washing, gently squeeze excess water from your hair with a microfiber towel or cotton T-shirt instead of rubbing, which can create unnecessary friction and frizz. Step 1: Apply Your Styling Products The best time to apply styling products is while your hair is still damp. Choose products based on the result you want to achieve: Custom Styling Primer helps protect against heat while smoothing the hair and reducing frizz. Formulated with provitamin B5 that provides color, UV, and heat protection (up to 450°F). Formulated for your unique hair goals with a personalized level of hold. Size: 6 oz Custom Hair Serum at the ends adds lightweight hydration and shine while helping smooth the hair cuticle. Formulated with sunflower seed oil and jojoba oil that smooths frizz, enhances shine, and protect hair from heat. The lightweight formula is fit for all hair types. Size: 3 oz Zero Gravity Mousse provides flexible volume and body without making hair feel stiff. Mousse adds volume, structure, and hold to a blowout. When activated by the heat of a blow dryer, its polymers expand to plump each hair strand and create lift at the roots. Distribute products evenly from mid-lengths to ends, adding mousse closer to the roots if you're looking for extra lift. Step 2: Rough Dry First Instead of immediately reaching for a round brush, begin by rough drying your hair until it's about 70-80% dry. Use your fingers to lift the roots while directing airflow downward. This removes excess moisture, shortens styling time, and reduces the amount of heat your hair experiences overall. Step 3: Choose the Right Tools Your technique matters, but so do your tools. Always use a concentrator nozzle on your blow dryer. Focused airflow helps smooth the cuticle for a shinier finish while giving you better control. Choose your brush based on your styling goals: Large round brush: Creates volume and movement. Medium round brush: Adds body with soft bends. Paddle brush: Creates a sleek, smooth finish. Step 4: Work in Sections Divide your hair into manageable sections before styling. Working with smaller sections allows heat to reach each piece evenly while maintaining the tension needed for a smooth finish. Place your brush underneath each section and slowly pull through while following closely with your dryer. Keep the airflow moving from roots to ends to encourage the cuticle to lie flat. Continue until each section is completely dry before moving to the next. Step 5: Let Your Hair Cool Heat temporarily reshapes the hydrogen bonds inside your hair, but cooling is what helps set your style. After drying each section, leave it wrapped around the brush or pin it loosely for several seconds before releasing. This simple step helps improve volume, bounce, and longevity. Step 6: Finish Your Style Once your hair has completely cooled, finish with a few drops of Custom Hair Serum through the mid-lengths and ends for added shine and frizz control. If you want additional volume, gently lift your roots with your fingertips instead of adding more heat. Blowout Tips by Hair Type Straight Hair Use lightweight styling Zero Gravity Mousse in small amounts at the root to avoid weighing hair down and focus on creating lift at the roots for long-lasting volume. Wavy Hair Work in smaller sections to smooth the hair while preserving natural movement with your round brush after applying Zero Gravity Mousse at the root. Add Styling Primer to help minimize humidity-related frizz and hold your style. Curly Hair If you're creating a smooth blowout, allow curls to stretch gradually rather than forcing them straight in one pass. Working slowly helps reduce unnecessary heat exposure. Work in smaller sections to smooth the hair while preserving natural movement with your round brush after applying Zero Gravity Mousse at the root. Add Styling Primer to help minimize humidity-related frizz and hold your style. Coily Hair Begin with well-conditioned hair and use smaller sections with consistent tension. Taking your time creates smoother results while helping protect the hair's structure. Work in smaller sections to smooth the hair while preserving natural movement with your round brush after applying Zero Gravity Mousse at the root. Add Styling Primer to help minimize humidity-related frizz and hold your style. The Bottom Line A salon-worthy blowout isn't about using the highest heat or the most products. It's about understanding how your hair responds to moisture, heat, and styling. When you start with products personalized to your hair type and goals, protect your hair during styling, and use the right technique, you can create a smooth, voluminous blowout that lasts longer while helping keep your hair healthy over time.

items.title: Sweat, Sunscreen, and Scalp Buildup: A Hair Type Guide to Summer Scalp Care
items.summary: Summer doesn't just change how your hair looks and feels. It changes what's happening at the scalp. Sweat, sunscreen, extra time outdoors, and shifting wash schedules all affect your scalp first. How your scalp responds depends entirely on your hair type. The Science Behind Summer Scalp Care Every hair type has a different relationship with sebum, the natural oil your scalp produces. The shape of your hair fiber determines how easily that oil travels from root to end. During summer, heat, sweat, and sunscreen residue all interact with that process differently. Understanding your hair's structure is the difference between guessing at a routine and building one that works with your scalp instead. How to Remove Sunscreen, Sweat, and Build-up Sunscreen formulas are water-resistant and contain zinc oxide or waxes, so you may need to apply your hair type shampoo directly to your roots and let it sit for 2 to 3 minutes to thoroughly break down the residue. If you are still feeling like you have residue on your hair, repeat the shampoo and double cleanse. Double cleansing means shampooing your hair twice during the same wash. The first cleanse lifts away sweat, excess oil, sunscreen, and product buildup from the scalp. The second cleanse gives your scalp a deeper clean, allowing your shampoo to work more effectively and leaving your hair feeling fresher and more balanced. First Cleanse: Thoroughly wet your hair, then work a quarter-sized amount of shampoo between your palms before applying it to your scalp. Using your fingertips, gently massage for 30 to 60 seconds to loosen buildup and impurities. Rinse thoroughly. Second Cleanse: Apply a slightly smaller amount of shampoo to your scalp. Because the initial buildup has already been removed, you'll notice a richer lather. Continue massaging your scalp, allowing the lather to glide through the lengths of your hair as you rinse. Finish by rinsing until the water runs clear. Straight Hair: Managing Faster Oil Production Straight hair's flat, tightly aligned cuticle allows sebum to travel from root to tip with the least resistance of any hair type. That's one reason straight hair often looks naturally shiny. During summer, however, heat and increased perspiration can accelerate oil buildup, leaving the scalp feeling greasy sooner than usual. Double Wash with Straight Hair Shampoo to remove sweat and buildup without over-stripping the scalp. Double cleansing is highly beneficial for straight hair in the summer. Straight hair allows oils to travel easily from the scalp to the ends, causing it to look greasy faster, especially when combined with summer sweat, humidity, and sunscreen. The first wash breaks down buildup, and the second deeply cleanses your scalp. Follow with Straight Hair Conditioner to keep lengths soft without weighing down fine hair. If you're heat-styling to manage humidity, add a Custom Styling Primer to your routine. A custom styling primer is formulated with provitamin B5 that provides color, UV, and heat protection (up to 450°F), formulated for your unique hair goals with a personalized level of hold. Wavy Hair: Balancing Oily Roots and Dry Ends Wavy hair sits in the middle of the hair type spectrum. Oil can accumulate at the roots while the mid-lengths and ends remain dry. Summer sweat tends to collect at the scalp, which can flatten your wave pattern before the rest of your hair even feels affected. Cleanse with Wavy Hair Shampoo and follow with Wavy Hair Conditioner to balance moisture without weighing down your waves. For a midday or post-workout refresh, work a small amount of Zero Gravity Styling Mousse through damp roots. It helps reactivate wave definition without adding unnecessary buildup. Try the Zero Gravity Mousse here for 15% off with CODE: 15OFFMOUSSE Curly Hair: Preventing Layered Buildup Curly hair's bends slow the movement of sebum, so oily roots are rarely the biggest concern during summer. Buildup is. Sweat, sunscreen, and styling products can layer between wash days, leaving curls feeling coated instead of defined. Use Curly Hair Shampoo to lift away buildup, then follow with Curly Hair Conditioner to restore hydration and improve manageability. Between wash days, work a small amount of Super Shape Curl Cream through damp roots and lengths to refresh curl definition without needing a full wash. Coily Hair: Protecting the Scalp Between Washes Coily hair's tight coil pattern makes it the most difficult for sebum to travel from the scalp to the ends. That's why coily hair routines are often built around less frequent washing. During summer, however, longer intervals between washes allow sweat, sunscreen, and styling products to remain on the scalp longer. Coily Hair Shampoo is formulated to cleanse thoroughly without stripping away the moisture that coily hair depends on. Follow with Coily Hair Conditioner to restore softness and manageability. Maintaining your regular wash schedule, rather than extending time between washes to avoid dryness, helps keep your scalp healthy during the hottest months of the year. The Bottom Line Summer scalp care is about understanding how your hair's structure manages oil, sweat, and buildup, then building a routine that supports those needs. When you care for your scalp based on your hair type, you're creating the ideal foundation for hair that looks healthier, feels balanced, and performs at its best all season long. Take the hair quiz to discover your hair type and shop the collection designed specifically for it.

items.title: Why Does Hair Frizz in Summer? Hair Care Tips for Every Hair Type
items.summary: Humidity season is here, and if your hair has its own opinion about the weather, you're not imagining it. Frizz isn't a flaw — it's physics. And once you understand what's actually happening at the strand level, you can stop fighting your hair type and start working with it. Frizz Is Structural, Not Random Here is the science: Hair is made primarily of keratin, a strong structural protein that naturally absorbs and releases water. On humid days, keratin draws moisture from the air into the hair shaft. As the hair absorbs that extra water, it swells, temporarily changing the hydrogen bonds that help determine your hair's shape. If moisture enters unevenly, the cuticle can lift, leading to frizz, puffiness, or a loss of definition. How much this happens depends on your hair's structure, which is why straight, wavy, curly, and coily hair each respond differently to humidity. That's also why a one-size-fits-all anti-frizz product rarely works for everyone in the room. Straight hair, wavy hair, curly hair, and coily hair each let moisture in and let it out differently, which means each one needs a different defense. As hair type experts, this is the exact problem we built Function of Beauty around: structure-matched care, not guesswork. How Frizz Shows Up by Hair Type Straight hair lies closest to the scalp, so it tends to pick up humidity fast and go flat or limp rather than visibly frizzy, though flyaways are still frizz's cousin. Straight hair's sebum (its natural oil) distributes easily down the shaft, which is great for shine but means it can look greasy before it looks frizzy. Wavy hair sits between straight and curly. It has more volume than straight hair but less natural definition than curly hair, which makes it prone to both frizz and a kind of directionless puff when humidity hits. Curly hair has a curled hair shaft that affects how oil travels from root to tip. That uneven oil distribution is why curls can look dry and frizzy at the same time. It can be one or the other, or both, for a structural reason. Coily hair has the tightest curl pattern and the most cuticle separation, making it both the most porous and the most fragile hair type. Sebum can't really navigate those tight coils. This leaves the hair chronically dry. When dry, the outer layer (cuticle) lifts, allowing humidity from the air to enter the shaft, causing the strands to swell and expand Matching Your Hair Routine to Your Hair Structure This is why we created our Hair Type Collections. Every shampoo and conditioner, leave-in treatment, and mask is formulated with the unique characteristics of straight, wavy, curly, and coily hair in mind, helping each hair type respond better to humidity with the moisture, lightweight care, or nourishment it needs. Straight Hair Shampoo & Conditioner, with coconut water and avocado oil, are built to cleanse and hydrate without weighing strands down — because straight hair doesn't need heavy moisture, it needs balance. Wavy Hair Shampoo & Conditioner, with fermented rice water and argan oil, target the smooth-and-strengthen combo wavy hair needs to hold its shape instead of frizzing into a halo. Curly Hair Shampoo & Conditioner, with flaxseed extract and Brazilian pracaxi oil, hydrate while gently cleansing, which helps curls stay defined instead of fighting both dryness and frizz at once. Coily Hair Shampoo & Conditioner, with chia seeds and Jamaican black castor oil, deliver the intensive moisture coily hair needs from root to tip, since it can't rely on its own sebum to do that work. If you're curly or coily, this is also a great season to lean on our Co-Wash. It's gentler than a full shampoo and lighter than a conditioner, so it won't strip the moisture your curls are working hard to hold onto. We recommend alternating it with your shampoo to keep your scalp clean without over-drying your strands. Twice a week, for any hair type dealing with humidity-related dryness, our Hair Mask gives you a deeper dose of conditioning with ingredients like shea butter, jojoba ester, and argan oil that go to work for 5 to 10 minutes to help reinforce the cuticle layer that humidity loves to disrupt. The Last Line of Defense: Sealing It All In Once your cleanse-and-condition routine is structure-matched, the final step is locking that moisture in before it has a chance to escape or before outside humidity has a chance to get in. For most hair types, that means a styling product that seals the cuticle rather than just sitting on top of it. If you've got a specific frizz-prone day ahead of you — a wedding, a humid vacation, a big presentation and want something built around your exact hair goals, our Custom Hair Serum is formulated to reduce frizz by 70% and protect against thermal damage up to 400°F, with your choice of hair goals layered in. It's a nice option to have in your back pocket for the days your regular routine needs backup. The Takeaway Frizz isn't a sign your hair care routine is failing; it's your hair's structure responding to its environment exactly the way it's built to. The fix isn't more product; it's the right product for your specific hair type. That's the whole idea behind Function of Beauty: we don't guess at what your hair needs. We start with the structure and build from there. Take the quiz, find your hair type collection, and let your hair do less work fighting the humidity this summer.

items.title: Pool, Sun, and Salt Water: A Hair Type Expert's Guide to Summer Hair Survival
items.summary: Chlorine, salt water, and UV exposure can change the way your hair looks, feels, and behaves. The reason isn't random, and it affects every hair type. The way your hair responds to pool water, ocean water, and sun exposure depends on its hair type, cuticle structure, moisture retention patterns, and daily routine. Understanding those differences can help you build a routine that works with your hair instead of against it. Hair damage occurs when the protective, outer layer of your hair, also known as the cuticle, is compromised, leaving cracks in its exterior. Once cracked, the cuticle lifts, resulting in dull, dry, frizzy, or brittle hair. It can be a nightmare, but all hope is not lost! While you may not be able to completely repair hair that is already damaged, there are still plenty of steps you can take to help prevent it from happening in the future. Building Your Hair Type's Summer Defense The good news is that protecting your hair during the summer doesn't require a complicated routine. We created a bundle just for you: Summer Rescue Bundle. This 3-step smoothing system is designed to help improve the feel of rough, dry, and hard-to-manage hair. One of the factors that can contribute to these conditions is chlorine exposure, which can affect moisture balance and leave strands feeling coarse. Formulated with hydrating ingredients, this system helps support hydration at the cuticle level, restoring softness, strengthening hair, improving manageability, and making hair feel smoother. A few simple steps before and after swimming can help support moisture retention, improve manageability, and reduce the effects of repeated environmental exposure What Chlorine, Salt Water, and Sun Actually Do to Hair Hair is made primarily of protein called keratin and protected by an outer layer called the cuticle. The cuticle acts as the hair's first line of defense, helping regulate moisture retention and protecting the inner structure of the fiber. Chlorine weakens keratin, which is the structural protein that gives hair its elasticity, resulting in split ends and breakage. Exposure to saltwater and UV rays physically pulls moisture from your strands through osmosis, leaving them dehydrated. Salt acts as a sponge, pulling water out of the hair shaft, which gives it a parched, straw-like texture. When this happens, moisture can escape more easily, the hair surface may become rougher, and strands can appear drier, duller, or more prone to frizz. Color-treated hair may also experience faster fading when exposed to the sun and pool water. Using the right products can help reduce breakage and recover from the summer stressors that we put on our hair. The goal is to understand how your hair's structure responds to summer conditions and support it accordingly. Sun, Salt Water, and Chlorine Affect Every Hair Type Differently Hair type isn't just how your hair looks. It's how it functions. The shape of the hair fiber influences how oils travel, how moisture is retained, and how the hair responds to environmental stressors like chlorine, UV exposure, humidity, and salt water. Straight Hair To protect and repair straight hair from chlorine and saltwater, focus on lightweight hydration and smoothing the cuticle. Straight hair shows structural damage quickly through frizz, limpness, and a straw-like texture, but it also weighs down easily if you use products that are too heavy. Avoid rubbing your hair with heavy beach towels, which roughs up the hair cuticle and causes extreme frizz. Instead, gently blot your hair or wrap it in a soft microfiber towel or cotton t-shirt. Wavy Hair Wavy hair (Type 2) sits between straight and curly hair in terms of moisture distribution. The bends in the hair strand make it slightly harder for oils to travel evenly, which can make waves more susceptible to frizz and moisture loss during the summer months. Sun exposure, chlorine, and humidity can disrupt wave definition, leaving hair looking less uniform and more prone to expansion. For wavy hair, protecting your pattern means balancing heavy moisture retention with curl-safe detangling. Wavy hair is naturally more porous and prone to frizz than straight hair, meaning chlorine and salt water can completely flatten your wave definition and turn your texture coarse or stringy. Curly Hair Curly hair (Type 3) naturally experiences greater challenges with moisture distribution because oils must travel around multiple curves and bends in the hair fiber. Protecting your curls from chlorine and saltwater is all about maximizing moisture barriers and preventing severe shrinkage and matting. Curly hair (Type 3) is naturally highly porous, meaning it absorbs damaging pool chemicals and salt like a sponge, leading to extreme frizz and hair damage. Coily Hair Coily hair (Type 4) has the most complex strand geometry of all hair types, making moisture retention especially important. Because natural oils have the hardest time traveling from root to end, coily hair often relies heavily on conditioning and moisture-focused routines to maintain softness and manageability. After swimming or prolonged sun exposure, coily hair may experience increased dryness and require additional hydration to help support the cuticle and maintain moisture balance. 4-Step Pre-swim Prep Routine before stepping into the water: Saturate with fresh water: Soak your hair completely under a tap or beach shower. Hair acts like a sponge; filling it with clean water prevents it from absorbing chemical pool water or drying salt water. Apply a leave-in conditioner: Coat your damp strands from roots to tips to create a water-resistant barrier. Use a leave-in conditioner built for your hair type. Put hair in a protective style: Secure your hair to minimize water friction, tangles, and matting. Use a high bun for straight hair, loose braids for wavy hair, and tight twists for curly hair. Wear a silicone swim cap: For the ultimate protection, tuck your prepped hair inside a silicone swim cap. This physically blocks the majority of the water from ever touching your strands. The best summer routine isn't about fighting your hair. It's about supporting the way your hair naturally functions so it can better withstand everything summer throws at it. Post-swim Routine for Your Hair Type (Straight, Curly, Coily, Wavy) Straight Hair: Focus on Cleansing With Lightweight Moisture Straight hair typically distributes natural oils more efficiently from root to end, which helps support shine and smoothness. After repeated swims and frequent washing, however, that natural lubrication can be reduced, leaving hair looking duller or feeling dry at the ends. After swimming, cleanse with the Straight Hair Shampoo to remove chlorine, salt, sunscreen, and buildup without stripping moisture. Follow with the Straight Hair Conditioner, formulated with coconut water and avocado oil to help support softness and shine. If you're spending extended time outdoors, apply Custom Styling Primer before styling to help provide heat and UV protection. Formulated with a Style Defense Complex that protects against heat and UV up to 450°F, with your choice of hair goals built in. Delivers up to 24 hours of humidity and frizz control without leaving a crunchy texture.Color & UV Defense: Formulated with rice seed protein to defend hair color from fading and protect strands from sun-induced UV damage. Wavy Hair: Focus on Moisture Balance and Definition Wavy hair sits in the middle of the moisture spectrum. It can become oily at the roots while still experiencing dryness through the mid-lengths and ends. Summer conditions often amplify frizz and make waves lose their natural definition. After swimming, use the Wavy Hair Shampoo to gently cleanse away chlorine and saltwater residue. Follow with the Wavy Hair Conditioner, featuring fermented rice water and argan oil to help support hydration without weighing waves down. For styling, apply Zero Gravity Styling Mousse to damp hair. Our lightweight foam mousse creates a flexible hold that's never crunchy, enhances the volume of your natural waves while keeping hair frizz-free. Aloe juice and apple extract help encourage wave definition while reducing the puffiness that often follows a day in the sun or water. Curly Hair: Focus on Moisture Retention and Curl Definition Curly hair naturally experiences greater challenges with moisture distribution because oils must travel around bends and curves throughout the strand. When chlorine, salt water, and sun exposure enter the equation, curls may feel drier, less defined, and more prone to tangling. After swimming, cleanse with the Curly Hair Shampoo and follow with the Curly Hair Conditioner. Ingredients like flaxseed and Brazilian pracaxi oil help support hydration and manageability while encouraging curl definition. To help curls recover after a day in the water, apply Super Shape Curl Cream to damp hair. Moringa oil and sugarcane help support curl formation while improving softness and reducing tangles. Coily Hair: Focus on Hydration and Recovery Coily hair has the most complex strand geometry, making moisture retention a priority year-round. After swimming, cleanse with the Coily Hair Shampoo and follow with the Coily Hair Conditioner, formulated with chia seed and Jamaican black castor oil to help support hydration and softness. Between wash days, use the Custom Co-Wash to gently cleanse the scalp and hair without removing the moisture your coils need to stay manageable. Formulated with Jamaican black castor seed oil and avocado oil, this co-wash moisturizes and protects coily, curly, and color-treated hair. If you'll be spending long days outdoors, apply Super Shape Curl Creme before going into the elements. Our Curly Hair Super Shape Curl Cream defines and hydrates curls with a flexible, touchable hold that never feels crunchy or sticky. This lightweight, plant-based cream enhances your natural curl pattern while reducing frizz and boosting elasticity for smooth, bouncy curls that last. items.title: Splitting Hairs: How to Treat 4 Types of Split Ends
items.summary: If you ask any hair stylist about the most common hair complaint they hear from clients, there’s a good chance it’s split ends. The annoying feather-effect they have on the ends of hair strands is anything but glamorous. Split ends can make hair look overwhelmed with frizz, dryness, and damage — definitely not words to describe healthy hair. While it might sound like we’re splitting hairs here, the truth is that there are different types of split ends. Each type indicates a different level and severity of hair damage. Luckily, there are ways to prevent, reduce, and alleviate split ends. Here’s what you need to know. The 4 Types of Split Ends As much as we don’t like to admit it, there's something kind of fascinating about split ends. Sure, they’re annoying and unsightly, but at the same time, examining the nitty-gritty details of a split end is like looking at your blackheads in a magnifying mirror. You hate that they're there yet you can't look away. Since we know you're curious about what can cause split ends and how you can get rid of them, let's investigate the four common types of split ends. Then, you can then begin to address the issues behind them. 1. Y-Split This is the prototypical split end. It looks like a "Y" where two separate sections have each split about 1/4" or more from each other. Y-split ends indicate the beginning stages of hair splitting, and are generally a sign of mild hair damage. Fortunately, you can give these types of split ends a softer look and feel with proper hydration. Pro Tip: Follow these 16 tips on how to moisturize hair 2. Feathered A hair strand with feathered split ends will look like a tree branch that has a bunch of twigs attached to it. Each split will vary in length, up to half an inch. Feathered split ends are an indicator of severely damaged hair. If you find a lot of feathered splits in your hair, this is a sign that your hair cuticles need some serious TLC. Pro Tip: Get a primer on hair cuticles to help tame your split ends 3. Candle This type of split end looks like a candlestick with a lit flame. The candlestick part of the hair shaft is as thick as the rest of the hair strands while the flame part appears to be about half the width of that. This is because the tip of the hair strand has been eroded, making it look like an entire layer of the cuticle has been peeled away. When this type of split end is grown out, it can make the strands weaker and thinner. Pro Tip: Check out these hacks for making thin hair look thicker 4. Single-Strand Knots This type of split end looks like a piece of rope that’s tied in a knot. Single-strand knots are usually caused by aggressive treatment of hair and are more common for those with coily or curly hair types. When a knot is formed in the hair, it makes detangling much harder. Oftentimes, when a brush or comb is run through dry hair, breakage occurs. Pro Tip: Learn how to avoid curly hair mistakes What Do Split Ends Say About Your Hair? No matter what kind of split ends you have, they’re all indicators that you have some degree of hair damage that needs to be addressed. Here’s what you need to know about haircare habits that might be causing your ends to split and what approach you can take to free yourself from split end stress. Your Heat Setting Are Too High You don't need to be a cosmetologist to know that heat styling tools can lead to frizzy hair, damage, and yes, split ends. But did you know that the duration, temperature, and proximity at which you style your hair is what affects your strands the most? In a study on hair shaft damage from hair dryers, different groups were tested to see how air drying affected their hair versus blow drying. For the blow-drying group, it was found that the longer and hotter the hair was treated, the more splitting occurred. However, those who used a continuous motion and held the blow dryer six inches away from their head tended to have less hair splitting and breakage than naturally dried hair. So what does this say? It says that hot tools can lead to split ends. But it also shows that using them on a consistent basis and at high temperatures is the real culprit. If you want to continue using blow-dryers and straighteners, do so with caution. Limit usage to once or twice a month and use products with heat protectant properties, such as Function of Beauty's custom hair serum. This lightweight serum can be used on damp or wet hair to help increase shine, smoothness and hydration. It's also been shown to: Reduce frizz by 70% Improve detangling by 75% Thermally protect hair up to 400 degrees You Need a Haircut No matter what types of split ends you have, these damaging dead ends have no place in your hair. Letting them stick around can wreak major havoc on your locks. The more stress and friction you enforce on your split ends, the more likely they’ll spread damage and splittage to the mid-length sections of your hair. To put an end to this, you need to get regular trims. It's simple but true. The best way to get rid of split ends is to cut them off at the source. As soon as your see splits start to form, head to the salon and snip away. If you catch them in the early stage of development, you'll probably only have to trim off a quarter-inch or so. This option is much better than having to cut off multiple inches because you've let your damage run the ends of your hair ragged. Regular trims are especially helpful if your dreams of growing long hair are being cut short by nasty split ends. Pro Tip: Learn how a haircut can change your hair for the better Too Much Shampooing, Not Enough Conditioning Washing your hair with shampoo too often can cause abrasion to the surface of your hair. However, conditioning can help protect the surface of your hair fibers and prevent damage from destructive grooming and chemical treatment habits. Plus, the protein-derived substances used in conditioners can help temporarily reduce the look of split ends. Since conditioning is such an important factor in protecting your hair from damage, consider adding a leave-in conditioner to your hair care routine. You can use it post-shower or apply it to dry hair to help smooth out the frizzy look that split ends can create. Function of Beauty's custom leave-in treatment gives split end-prone hair a much needed dose of shine and hydration thanks to naturally derived and synthetic ingredients like avocado oil, argan oil, and coffee extract. It’s Time to Get a Handle on Your Split Ends Having a few (or even a lot) of split ends doesn't mean you're doomed to a life of flyaways and frizz. It just means that you need to change up your hair habits and find the right hair products to help mask them. Using lower temperatures when heat styling, adding a leave-in conditioner to your haircare routine, and trimming your split ends as soon as they pop up will help you keep your split ends in check and prevent future ones from popping up. items.title: Sweet Almond Oil for Hair: Don't Miss Out on These 4 Benefits
items.summary: When it comes to adding hair oils to your hair care routine, you may want to give sweet almond oil a try. Sure, coconut oil gets lots of love for its nourishing and moisturizing capabilities. But its rich oily texture is best reserved for drier and coarse hair types. Meanwhile, sweet almond oil is lighter in texture without compromising on hydration. That's why it's a universally appealing oil for all hair types. But what are the exact benefits of sweet almond oil for hair? And how can you use it to make your mane gloriously luscious? Read on for the answers to your most-asked questions. Sweet Almond Oil for Hair: Back to Its Roots Did you know there are two types of almond oils: sweet almond oil and bitter almond oil? Due to sweet almond oil's beauty benefits, it's often found in skincare and haircare products, which is why it's the star of this article. Sweet almond oil is extracted from the kernels of ripened sweet almonds. The almond tree (Prunus dulcis) is native to Asia and the Middle East, and its fruits were documented as early as 780,000 B.C.E. Today, America is the largest almond producer in the world, specifically the state of California. In terms of hair care, the the profile of sweet almond oil is pretty impressive as it's infused with: Omega fatty acids, like oleic acid, linoleic acid, and palmitic acid Vitamin E, which is a fat-soluble antioxidant Essential minerals, including potassium, phosphorus, calcium, and magnesium Polyphenols, which have antioxidant properties You should also know that cold-pressed sweet almond oil is considered unrefined, as it retains more of its beneficial nutrients. On the other hand, refined sweet almond oil usually undergoes some form of heat and/or chemical processing to extend its shelf life. 4 Benefits of Sweet Almond Oil for Hair OK, you are now an expert on the various nutrients sweet almond oil possesses. But how do they relate to the health of your hair? Mainly, in the following four ways. 1. An Incredible Softener for Rough Strands Because sweet almond oil is an incredible emollient at heart, it's the go-to softener for hair. ICYDK what emollients are, they are hydrating oils that fill in the gaps of your hair cuticles (the outermost protective layer of your hair shaft) to keep moisture in. Your cuticles have overlapping, scale-like cells to maintain optimal hydration levels, and the cuticles also protect the inner parts of the fiber (read: the cortex and the medulla). Healthy cuticles mean that every scale lies perfectly flat with little to no "pores" (aka low porosity hair). Unfortunately, external stressors like heat, chemicals, and friction raise the cuticle layer and create more pores than you would like. As a result, the uneven cuticles of high porosity hair lead to a roughened texture. This is where sweet almond oil helps your strands. Using its emollient superpowers, it fills in the pores for a smoother cuticle and seals in moisture. Well-moisturized strands thus feel softer to the touch. 2. A Miracle Oil for Dull-Looking Hair The cuticle-smoothing ability of sweet almond oil also works wonders to create glossy-looking hair. That's because flatter, smoother cuticles do a better job of reflecting light and the oil creates a glossy film on your fibers to supercharge their natural radiance. As you can imagine, this two-way approach makes your hair shinier than ever. 3. A Formidable Tamer for Frizz and Flyaways One of the major benefits of almond oil is that it helps tone down unwanted frizz and flyaways. But first, let's look behind the scenes to understand why your hair turns frizzy. When your hair cuticles are peppered with pores, your mane loses more moisture than it retains. This leads to insufficient lipids in your hair shafts (think ceramides, cholesterol, and fatty acids). Unfortunately, these internal hair lipids cannot be replenished through your scalp's natural oils. In an attempt to compensate for the increased dryness, your fibers absorb the surrounding water droplets in the air. This causes your hair shafts to swell and frizz. So, how can you restore the internal moisture levels of your fibers without the dreaded frizz? The answer: sweet almond oil. As we've mentioned, sweet almond oil contains omega-3 fatty acids, which is part of your fibers' natural lipid profile. Applying the oil to your tresses helps restock your inner hair oils sans the frizz. Aside from using sweet almond oil straight from the bottle as a natural moisturizer for dry hair and dry scalp, look for hair products that contain it as an ingredient. For example, you can add the "volumize" hair goal to your Function of Beauty custom shampoo and conditioner. 4. A Friction-Reducing Balm for Hair Breakage We all know that combs and tangled hair don't mix well — can you say unwanted breakage and split ends? But sweet almond oil can help eliminate the struggle of knots and snarls. One study involving Brazilian oils and butters found that the botanically derived oils: Increased the ease of combing wet hair Significantly enhanced hair gloss Reduced the risk of split ends In other words, applying sweet almond oil (also a plant-based oil) to your strands makes hair brushing a breeze, and puts you closer to achieving that healthy hair look. How to Use Sweet Almond Oil for Hair Just like other lightweight carrier oils — think jojoba and olive oils — you can use sweet almond oil on its own or mixed with essential oils. How to use sweet almond oil on its own: Rub a few drops of sweet almond oil between your palms to warm up the oil. Apply the oil to your hair with your hands in a praying motion from the mid-length down. If you're struggling with dry skin on your scalp, apply the oil from roots to tips. Gently brush through your mane with a wide tooth comb to minimize breakage and ensure every strand is evenly coated with the oil. This is a good time to work out the kinks. Leave the oil on for at least 30 minutes before shampooing. If you have an oily scalp, start with only 1-2 drops of sweet almond oil and concentrate it on the ends of your hair. This way, you can let the oil hydrate your locks without risking too much product buildup. How to use sweet almond oil as a DIY hair mask: Peel and remove the pit of one ripe avocado, then mash it thoroughly Combine coconut oil and sweet almond oil in a mixing bowl in a 2:1 ratio Add the mashed avocado to the bowl and mix well Apply the mixture to damp hair from the roots to the tips Let the mask sit for 30 minutes before rinsing it off with water Follow up with your usual shampoo and conditioner routine Because sweet almond oil is such an easy haircare ingredient to play with, you can easily mix and match with other hair-healthy ingredients. For example, you can swap out avocado and coconut oil for lightweight ingredients like honey and yogurt. Reap the Fruits of Sweet Almond Oil for Hair Sweet almond oil for hair is one of the best ways to treat your tresses. After all, who doesn't want to get rid of too-rough strands, dullness, frizz, and split ends? You can go the DIY route (which we've listed above) or choose hair products infused with sweet almond oil — the latter is great if you simply want convenience. To see sweet almond oil on the ingredient list of your haircare products, choose the "volumize" hair goal when you take our hair quiz. It's time to reap the fruits of sweet almond oil for hair.

items.title: Winter Hair Care Tips: How to Prevent Dry Hair, Static, and Breakage
items.summary: Winter changes how your hair behaves. Nothing about winter hair behavior is random. Its structure responds to its environment. If your hair feels drier, frizzier, or more prone to static during winter, nothing is "wrong" with it. It's simply responding to its environment. Hair fibers naturally exchange moisture with the air around them. During winter, cold air holds less moisture, and indoor heating further reduces humidity levels. In low-humidity environments, dry air seeks moisture equilibrium and naturally draws water out from the inner hair fiber (the cortex). This moisture loss causes the protective outer layer (the cuticle) to lift. As the hair fiber dehydrates, the outer cuticle layer becomes rigid, raised, and rough, leading directly to dullness, static, frizz, and breakage. The good news? A few strategic adjustments can help support your hair's structure and keep it performing at its best all season long. Why Does Hair Get Dry in Winter? Dryness is not random. It is structural. Your hair's cuticle acts as a protective barrier that controls moisture exchange between the hair fiber and the environment. During winter, low humidity, indoor heating, and temperature fluctuations can cause moisture to leave the hair more quickly than it can be replenished. As moisture levels decrease, the cuticle becomes rougher and less effective at retaining hydration. This can lead to: Dryness Frizz Static Dullness Increased breakage Protecting moisture retention becomes one of the most important goals of a winter hair care routine. 1. Protect Hair From Cold Weather Hats, scarves, and hoods don't just keep you warm. They help shield your hair from cold air, wind, and moisture loss. Satin-lined or silk-lined hats are the best way to prevent damage and lock in moisture. The smooth surface prevents friction and eliminates static 2. Never Go Outside With Wet Hair Wet hair is more vulnerable to stress because the hair fiber swells when it absorbs water. When hair is swollen, the internal bonds that help maintain its structure become easier to stretch and disrupt. Combined with cold temperatures, this can increase the likelihood of breakage and roughness. Allow your hair to dry completely before heading outdoors whenever possible. 3. Fight Winter Static by Supporting Moisture Balance Static is not a flaw. It's physics acting on dry fiber. When humidity levels drop, electrical charges build more easily on the hair shaft. Friction from hats, scarves, sweaters, and brushes transfers electrons to the hair, causing strands to repel one another and creating flyaways and static. For straight and wavy hair, a personalized Leave-In Conditioner can help replenish moisture while smoothing the cuticle. Following with a Custom Hair Serum helps create a lightweight barrier that seals in hydration, reduces friction, and minimizes static buildup throughout the day. For curly and coily hair, Function of Beauty Super Shape Curl Cream for Curly Hair can provide additional moisture retention and cuticle support while helping curls stay defined and aligned in dry winter conditions. 4. Wash With Lukewarm Water Hot showers feel great in winter, but excessive heat can accelerate moisture loss from the hair fiber. Washing with lukewarm water helps cleanse the hair while preserving more of the moisture needed for softness, flexibility, and shine. Cooler rinses may also help support a smoother cuticle surface, which can improve light reflection and overall shine. 5. Use a Humidifier Indoors Indoor heating systems dramatically reduce moisture levels in the air. A humidifier helps restore humidity to your environment, reducing the amount of moisture drawn from your hair and skin throughout the day. Think of it as supporting your hair before you even step into the shower. 6. Switch to a Microfiber Towel Traditional bath towels can create friction that roughens the cuticle and increases breakage. Instead, gently blot excess water using a microfiber towel or soft cotton T-shirt. Less friction helps maintain a smoother cuticle and reduces unnecessary stress on the hair fiber. 7. Extend Time Between Washes Natural oils help lubricate the hair shaft and support moisture retention. Because winter conditions can already leave hair feeling drier, extending time between wash days may help preserve some of the scalp's natural protective oils. If your hair and scalp tolerate it, consider washing less frequently during colder months. 8. Deep Condition Weekly When winter air pulls moisture from the hair fiber, restoring hydration becomes essential. A weekly Hair Mask helps support moisture retention by conditioning the cuticle and improving the hair's ability to hold onto hydration. This is especially important for curly, coily, color-treated, or high-porosity hair, which naturally loses moisture more quickly. Consistent deep conditioning can help improve softness, manageability, and resilience throughout the season. 9. Reduce Heat Styling and Use a Heat Protectant Hair that is already experiencing seasonal moisture loss may be more vulnerable to heat-related stress. Heat styling repeatedly disrupts hydrogen bonds inside the hair fiber and can contribute to cuticle wear over time. Function of Beauty recommends using a styling primer formulated with provitamin B5 that provides color, UV, and heat protection (up to 450°F). Formulated for your unique hair goals with a personalized level of hold. Whenever possible, embrace your natural texture or reduce styling temperatures. If heat styling is part of your routine, apply a personalized Styling Primer beforehand to help support the hair fiber and reduce thermal stress during styling. 10. Personalize Your Routine for Your Hair Type Every hair type responds differently to winter. Straight hair often benefits from lightweight hydration and moisture retention without added weight. Wavy hair typically needs balanced moisture and frizz management. Curly hair benefits from increased moisture support because natural oils have a harder time traveling through bends and curves in the hair shaft. Coily hair often requires deeper hydration and moisture retention because its structure creates more opportunities for moisture loss along the fiber. Because every hair type has a different architecture, the most effective winter routine is one designed around your unique hair structure and behavior. Shop your hair type HERE. The Bottom Line Winter hair challenges are the result of changing humidity, moisture movement, and environmental stressors. Focusing on moisture retention, minimizing friction, supporting the cuticle, and protecting the internal structure of the hair fiber can help you reduce dryness, static, and breakage throughout the season. items.summary: We've all experienced the frustration of dealing with unruly, frizzy hair at some point. Whether it's due to humidity, dryness, or damage, frizz can turn a good hair day into a battle against the elements. But that’s why we’re here, to offer you some understanding and solutions to the dreaded frizz. The Culprits: What Causes Hair to Frizz Humidity Induced Frizz Imagine a damp day, and your hair seems to have a mind of its own, puffing up in all directions. This phenomenon is the result of humidity-induced frizz. Hair acts like a sponge, absorbing moisture from the air, causing the strands to swell and become porous. Porous hair is particularly susceptible to frizz as the cuticle layer lifts, leading to a rough and unruly appearance. Dryness Induced Frizz On the opposite end of the spectrum is dryness-induced frizz. Hair that lacks sufficient moisture becomes dehydrated and loses its natural oils, making the cuticle layer rough and susceptible to frizz. The lack of moisture also causes individual strands to stand out, giving hair that unmistakably frizzy appearance. Damage Induced Frizz Chemical treatments, excessive heat styling, and environmental stressors can all damage the hair's structure, making it prone to frizz. When the hair's cuticle layer is compromised, it loses its ability to lay flat and smooth. Damaged hair lacks the structural integrity necessary to repel moisture and environmental factors, exacerbating frizz issues. Solutions: How to Keep Frizz at Bay Humidity-Defying Strategies To combat humidity-induced frizz, the key is sealing the hair's cuticle and minimizing moisture absorption. Using anti-humidity hair products, such as serums and sprays, can provide a protective barrier against excess moisture. Look for products that contain ingredients like silicones and natural oils, which help to repel water and keep the hair smooth. Hydration for Dry Hair For dryness-induced frizz, restoring moisture is paramount. Incorporate a hydrating shampoo and conditioner into your hair care routine. Deep conditioning treatments or hair masks enriched with ingredients like shea butter, argan oil, or glycerin can replenish lost moisture, making the hair more manageable and less prone to frizz. Repairing Damaged Hair Damaged-induced frizz calls for a comprehensive hair repair approach. Start by trimming off split ends to prevent further damage from traveling up the hair shaft. Use protein-rich hair treatments to rebuild the hair's structure and strengthen its overall health. Additionally, opt for sulfate-free shampoos and mild, nourishing conditioners to minimize further damage. CUSTOMIZE YOUR ROUTINE Our number one tip to tame frizzy hair? Our Custom Hair Serum :) It’s a comprehensive solution to combat all types of frizz. The secret lies in its unique blend of ingredients, carefully formulated to address the core issues of frizz. With built-in thermal protection of up to 400°F, this serum shields your hair from the damaging effects of heat styling tools. Its lightweight formula seals the hair cuticles, preventing excess moisture from penetrating, while also locking in essential hydration. items.title: Best Vitamins for Hair Health: 11 Nutrients That Support Stronger, Healthier Hair
items.summary: Disclaimer: The information provided is not intended as medical advice. For any medical concerns, always contact your doctor or dermatologist.When it comes to healthy hair, what you put on your plate matters just as much as the products you apply to your strands. After all, the scalp is home to around 100,000 hair follicles, and each one relies on a steady supply of nutrients to function at its best. While there’s no single vitamin guaranteed to give you longer, thicker hair overnight, a balanced diet can help support healthy hair growth, strength, and shine.It's also worth noting that more isn't always better. Experts agree that vitamins and supplements shouldn't replace a nutritious diet, and taking high doses of certain nutrients may do more harm than good. If you're concerned that you may not be getting enough of a particular nutrient, don't self-diagnose based on internet searches alone. Nutrient deficiencies should be confirmed through proper medical evaluation and testing. Before adding supplements to your routine, talk with your doctor or dermatologist to determine whether a deficiency is actually present and what treatment approach is right for you. 11 Nutrients and Vitamins for Hair 11 Nutrients and Vitamins for Healthy HairHealthy hair looks different for everyone, whether you have sleek straight strands, voluminous curls, or textured coils. But regardless of your hair type, strong, resilient strands start with proper nourishment. 2. Vitamin A Vitamin A supports normal cell growth throughout the body, including the cells that make up your hair and scalp. Foods rich in vitamin A include: Sweet potatoes, carrots, spinach, kale, butternut squash, cantaloupe, and eggs. 2. Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) Riboflavin helps convert food into energy and supports normal cellular function. Because healthy hair growth requires a constant supply of energy, this B vitamin plays a supporting role in maintaining healthy strands. Foods rich in riboflavin include: Milk, yogurt, eggs, salmon, lean beef, mushrooms, almonds, spinach. 3. Vitamin B7 (Biotin) Biotin has become one of the most talked-about nutrients for hair health, but if you aren’t deficient, it won’t help much. It’s involved in the production of keratin, the protein that makes up hair, skin and nails. Foods rich in biotin include: Eggs, salmon, avocados, sweet potatoes, sunflower seeds, almonds, beef liver. 4. Vitamin B9 (Folate or Folic Acid) Folate helps support healthy cell growth and renewal, making it an important nutrient for tissues throughout the body—including the scalp. Foods rich in folate include: Lentils, chickpeas, black beans, spinach, asparagus, Brussels sprouts, and avocados. 5. Vitamin C Vitamin C is an antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress. It also supports collagen production, a structural protein found throughout the body. Foods rich in vitamin C include: Oranges, grapefruit, strawberries, kiwi, bell peppers, broccoli, and Brussels sprouts. 6. Vitamin D Vitamin D plays a role in many bodily functions, including supporting healthy skin and scalp health. While sunlight helps your body produce vitamin D naturally, certain foods can help you meet your daily needs as well. Sources of vitamin D include: Salmon, sardines, egg yolks, fortified milk, fortified cereals, and UV-exposed mushrooms. 7. Vitamin E As an antioxidant, vitamin E helps protect cells from oxidative damage and supports overall skin and scalp health. Foods rich in vitamin E include: Almonds, sunflower seeds, hazelnuts, peanuts, avocados, spinach, and olive oil. 8. Protein and Collagen-Supporting Nutrients Hair is primarily made of keratin, a protein. That’s why consuming enough protein is one ef the most important dietary habits for maintaining healthy hair. Protein-rich foods include: Chicken, turkey, fish, eggs, Greek yogurt, lentils, tofu, and tempeh.For additional collagen support, pair protein-rich foods with vitamin C-rich fruits and vegetables. 9. Omega-3 Fatty Acids Omega-3 fatty acids help support scalp health and contribute to overall skin hydration. Since the body cannot product them on its own, they need to come from food. Foods rich in omega-3s include: Salmon, mackerel, sardines, herring, chia seeds, flaxseeds, walnuts. 10. Iron Iron helps transport oxygen throughout the body, including the the tissues that support healthy hair growth. Foods rich in iron include: Lean red meat, oysters, lentils, beans, spinach, pumpkin seeds, fortified cereals 11. Selenium Selenium supports several important functions in the body, including healthy thyroid function and antioxidant activity. Foods rich in selenium include: Brazil nuts, tuna, sardines, shrimp, eggs, brown rice, and whole grains. That’s where Function of Beauty’s 100% custom-made formulations come in handy. items.summary: Key Takeaways Thin hair and thinning hair are different. Thinning hair refers to a reduction in hair density over time, while thin hair is often determined by genetics. The right haircut can create the appearance of more volume. Layers, bobs, pixie cuts, and strategic shaping help build movement and dimension. Hair density influences how full hair appears. Volume is often determined by both the number of hairs on the scalp and the way hair is cut and styled. Lightweight products help support volume. Volumizing shampoos, conditioners, leave-ins, and styling products can help prevent hair from becoming weighed down. Scalp health and hair care habits matter. Heat styling, tight hairstyles, product buildup, and environmental stressors can influence how hair looks and behaves over time.

items.title: The Best Hair Oils for Every Hair Type: Benefits, Uses, and How to Choose the Right One
items.summary: Key Takeaways Not all hair oils work the same way. Different oils vary in weight, absorption, and how they support moisture retention and hair manageability. Hair oils help support the cuticle. A smoother cuticle can improve shine, reduce friction, and help minimize frizz and breakage. Hair type influences which oil works best. Thick, coarse, curly, and coily hair often benefit from richer oils, while fine or oily hair may prefer lightweight options. Oils support moisture retention, but they don't add water to the hair. Their primary role is helping seal and protect moisture already present in the hair fiber. The best hair oil is the one suited to your hair's structure and needs. Personalized routines help ensure your products support your unique hair type, environment, and goals.

items.title: Hair Type Guide: How to Identify Your Hair Type, Porosity, Density, and Scalp Needs
items.summary: Key Takeaways Hair type is more than curl pattern. Texture, density, porosity, strand thickness, and scalp health all influence how your hair behaves. Every hair type has a unique structure. Straight, wavy, curly, and coily hair each have different moisture, styling, and maintenance needs. Porosity affects moisture movement. Hair's ability to absorb and retain moisture plays a major role in dryness, frizz, and product performance. Scalp health influences hair health. Oil production, moisture balance, and scalp condition help shape how your hair looks and feels. The best routine is personalized. Understanding your hair's unique architecture helps you choose products and techniques that support healthier-looking hair.

items.title: Ingredient of the Month: Rose Extract
items.summary: The Ingredient of the Month series highlights one of our meticulously-selected ingredients. Get to know them all on our newly-launched Ingredients Page. Welcome back to another installment of Ingredient of the Month. This time around we’re highlighting one of our most beloved ingredients — rose extract. Found in multiple best-selling Function of Beauty formulas, rose extract offers an array of notable benefits for the hair that you should know about. Here, everything you need to know about rose extract. Main benefits: Delivers moisture to the hair, helps prevent split ends, balances excess oil + flakes GOALS: fix split ends hair goal for custom hair serum + custom leave-in Widely renowned for its highly therapeutic benefits, rose extract is a time-tested ingredient commonly used in a variety of personal care products — from serums and moisturizers, to shampoo and conditioner. Rich in vitamins A, C, D, and E, as well as essential fatty acids, rose extract is a powerful antioxidant with both soothing and hydrating properties. Moreover, it can help balance oil on the face or scalp. When it comes to the hair, specifically, rose extract aids in preventing split ends, delivering deep moisture to dry frizzy strands, and keeping oil under control. Rose extract also has a stunning floral scent profile, which makes it an excellent ingredient to use in natural fragrances. Currently, you can find rose extract in our hair serum and leave-in formulas. It’s worth noting that we use a synthetic form of rose because, believe it or not, producing a single pound of rose essential oil can take roughly 10,000 pounds of rose petals. Pretty wild, right? That’s why we went the synthetic route, to help sustain our Earth’s natural resources.

items.title: 6 Hair Color Ideas to Compliment You
items.summary: Switching up your hair color is always an exciting event, especially when you’re entering into a new season of your life. If you ask us, no change is more transformative to your overall look than your hair color. A new hue makes a bold statement about who you are and what you want to become. But committing to a new color can be intimidating. Where do you even begin in your search for the perfect hue? If you’re in need of hair color ideas that complement your complexion and style, we’ve got you. From mega-dramatic tones that give you a whole new look to low-maintenance colors that suit your busy lifestyle, this guide offers hair color ideas that will work for you. Concerned about compromising the health of your hair? We’re also here to offer tips on maintaining your color and keeping your locks in prime condition. Best Hair Color Ideas: 6 Fabulous Options to Consider We firmly believe that any color can work for any person. If you want bright pink hair with blue highlights in a pixie cut, go for it! But there are some guidelines to help you choose the best hair color idea for your complexion ⁠— let’s explain. Most hair colors either lean towards warm or cool tones. The same goes for your skin tone. If you have yellow, gold, or peachy undertones, you have a warm complexion. If you have blue or pink undertones, your complexion is cool. Not sure which one describes you? Here’s a quick trick: Examine the color of the veins on your wrist to determine the type of complexion you have. Blue veins mean you have cool undertones and green veins mean you have warm undertones. For your hair and skin tone to complement each other, select a hair color that’s within your warm or cool color family. Let’s review six on-trend hair color ideas to see which ones might work for you. Chocolate Brown Chocolate brown is one of the richest, most beautiful hair shades out there. It looks amazing on those with warm golden skin tones and can bring out any eye color. Since this is such a dimensional shade, we’d only suggest it for those with a lot of time to commit to the chocolatey aesthetic. If your natural hair color is much lighter or darker than chocolate, you’ll need frequent touch-ups to maintain this rich hue. Pro Tip: Check out more brown hair color ideas. Bronde There’s a fine line between dirty blonde and light brown hair and it’s called bronde. This color blends blonde and brown tones to give you a trendy, low-maintenance look. Being “bronde” can truly work for everybody, so long as you choose the right shade for you. If you have naturally dark hair and are looking to go bronde, we’d first recommend getting darker blonde highlights. Choosing golden blonde or caramel highlights will give you a bronde look you can easily maintain when your dark roots grow out. For blondes wanting to go darker, ask your colorist for lowlights in brunette shades like mushroom or light golden brown. Gray The gray hair color trend can look modern, playful, and sophisticated all at the same time. Gray shades work best on those with cool undertones. If you’re looking to layer a gray tone over your current color, choose a shade close to your natural hue. If you have naturally lighter hair, go with a light lavender or silvery blonde hue. If your hair is naturally dark, a charcoal or blue-gray shade will flatter your tresses. Pro Tip: Explore more gray hair color ideas. Black Give your hairstyle the ultimate edge by dying it the darkest shade of all. Black hair is undeniably mysterious and dramatic, especially if you’ve been rocking lighter tresses for some time. If you’re not sure if this raven-toned hair color idea is for you, here are some things to consider. Paler complexions with cool undertones will find black hair to be more flattering than those with peachy, warm undertones who may find that this dark shade washes them out. If you have a medium to darker skin tone, your richer pigment allows you to pull off this dramatic shade well. If your complexion is rich in golden or yellow undertones, mix in mocha brown balayage highlights to add multidimensional warm tones to your tresses. Rose Gold The pastel hair trend is still having a moment, but this time it’s veering into natural tones with redhead-adjacent shades of rose gold. This color looks kind of like strawberry blonde but has more pinky elements to it, making it best for those with warm, golden, or peach undertones. If you want to experiment with this cotton candy shade, layer a rose gold ombre hair color over your locks or add some peekaboo hair highlights to the ends of your tresses. Pro Tip: Got redhead curiosity? Check out more red hair color ideas. Platinum Blonde Platinum blonde is an iconic shade that many desire but few have the guts to commit to. If you love this Barbie-like blonde hair color idea but are afraid you can’t pull it off, think again. Platinum naturally complements those with pale skin and light eyes, but having these features isn’t required to rock this cool blonde shade. If your skin has cool undertones (and you’re ready for all the attention this color is going to give you), go platinum! The biggest question and concern about going platinum is whether bleaching it will destroy one’s hair. The answer is yes ⁠— unless you take the right steps to prevent major damage. The bleaching process is toughest on black or brunette hair because the darker your natural hair color is, the more rounds of bleach you’ll have to go through to get it to platinum. So if you’re dead set on taking your dark hair to the lightest of light shades, you have to commit to routine TLC for your tresses. Pro Tip: Try a purple shampoo to preserve platinum color and combat brassy tones. How to Care for Color-Treated Hair The downside of committing to a new hair color is that it can come with some degree of hair damage. Hair dye works by penetrating hair cuticles to deposit or remove color in the cortex, causing swelling and some damage to the hair strands. Regular dye jobs can cause your hair to feel rough, dry, tangled, and frizzy. Luckily, using a hair mask can make your hair look and feel a lot better. Function of Beauty’s customized hair mask is made to help replenish color damaged hair. It’s created with conditioning agents like argan oil, Japanese sake, and jojoba ester oil to give you more hydration than a traditional conditioner. Coat your strands with this product once or twice a week to improve softness and help restore the moisture your tresses need. Now That You’ve Found the Best Hair Color Idea ... With so many hair color ideas, it can be daunting to choose one. But once you know how to choose a hair tone that works with your complexion ⁠— and understand how much time it takes to keep up with color commitments ⁠— it’ll be much easier to decide on a perfect hue. To help maintain your new hair color, Function of Beauty has you covered. Take this hair quiz to build a custom shampoo and conditioner combo. This hair washing set can be optimized with goals such as color protection, which will prevent fading and enhance your strands for optimum color uptake and long lasting color.

items.title: Damaged Hair: Causes, Signs, and 9 Ways to Prevent Further Damage
items.summary: Key Takeaways Hair damage occurs when the protective cuticle layer becomes compromised by heat, friction, chemical treatments, environmental exposure, or harsh grooming habits. Common signs of damaged hair include dryness, frizz, dullness, split ends, breakage, rough texture, and increased tangling. Gentle hair care habits, including careful detangling and reducing unnecessary friction, can help minimize future damage. Heat styling, chemical processing, chlorine, salt water, and excessive brushing can all contribute to weakening the hair fiber over time. Hydration is essential for maintaining healthy-looking hair and helping improve softness, smoothness, and manageability. Deep conditioning treatments, leave-in conditioners, and heat protectants can help support the hair's moisture balance and protective barrier.
